name: Capacity Utilization
short: The share of total output capacity that is actually being used.
long: Compares actual output with the maximum output a resource or system could deliver over the same period. A high value can reveal efficient use, but sustained operation near the limit may leave too little protection against variability or maintenance.

name: Complete and On-Time Delivery
short: The share of orders delivered complete, in the correct quantity, and on time.
long: A customer-service KPI that succeeds only when the whole order arrives by the promised time and contains every required item in the right quantity. It is stricter than measuring timeliness alone.

name: Days of Supply
short: How many days current on-hand inventory can support expected usage.
long: Converts inventory units into time by dividing available inventory by an appropriate daily demand or usage rate. It helps planners judge coverage and compare items with different unit volumes.

name: Fill Rate
short: The percentage of requested units that can be supplied from available inventory.
long: Measures unit-level availability: units fulfilled directly from stock divided by units ordered. It differs from order fill rate, which judges whether each entire order was completed.

name: Forecast Accuracy
short: How closely a forecast matches the actual outcome.
long: A family of measures used to assess forecast quality. One common expression is one minus MAPE, but the chosen formula, aggregation level, horizon, and treatment of zero demand must be documented before comparing results.

name: Inventory Turnover
short: How many times average inventory is sold or consumed during a period.
long: Typically calculated as annual cost of sales divided by average inventory valued on the same basis. Higher turnover can indicate faster flow, although too little inventory may reduce service or resilience.

name: On-Time Delivery
short: The percentage of customer receipts that arrive on time.
long: Compares receipts meeting the agreed delivery date or window with total receipts. The business must define whether early deliveries count as on time and which timestamp and promise date are authoritative.

name: Order Fill Rate
short: The percentage of customer orders fulfilled completely.
long: An order-level service measure. An order counts as filled only when the complete requested order is supplied; a partly filled order does not pass, even when most individual units were available.

name: Perfect Order
short: An order delivered without error across product, quantity, condition, place, time, customer, and cost.
long: A composite view of order quality based on doing every important part of fulfillment correctly. Because every condition must pass, the measure exposes cross-functional problems that separate delivery, quality, and documentation metrics may hide.

name: Schedule Adherence
short: How closely production execution follows the authorized schedule.
long: Compares what was produced, in the intended quantity and timing, with the published schedule. The organization should define its time bucket, tolerance, freeze window, and whether sequence changes count as misses.

name: Backlog
short: Customer demand received but not yet fulfilled.
long: The quantity or value of accepted demand still waiting for delivery. Tracking backlog by age and promised date helps distinguish healthy future orders from overdue commitments.

name: Manufacturing Cycle Time
short: The elapsed time required to manufacture a product through the production process.
long: Measures the time from the start of manufacturing activity to completion. Its scope should state whether queue, move, inspection, setup, and packaging time are included so trends remain comparable.

name: Work in Process
short: Inventory that has entered production but is not yet a finished good.
long: Represents material currently being transformed or waiting between operations. Excess WIP can increase lead time, hide quality issues, consume space, and complicate priority management.

name: Master Schedule Stability
short: The degree to which the master production schedule remains unchanged within agreed time fences.
long: Tracks changes to planned quantities or timing, especially near execution. A stable schedule helps purchasing and production coordinate, while excessive rigidity may prevent a sensible response to real demand changes.

name: Supplier On-Time Delivery
short: The percentage of supplier receipts arriving by the agreed date or within the agreed window.
long: Evaluates inbound delivery reliability. The definition should specify requested versus confirmed date, early-delivery rules, delivery location, and whether partial receipts qualify.

name: Production Plan Attainment
short: Actual production compared with the approved production plan for the period.
long: Shows whether the organization delivered the aggregate output it committed to. It should be measured at a meaningful family and time-bucket level and interpreted with mix, inventory, and demand changes.

name: Scrap Rate
short: The proportion of production output or material that cannot be recovered as conforming product.
long: Measures loss caused by unusable production. It may be expressed in units, weight, or cost, but numerator and denominator must use compatible bases and distinguish scrap from rework.

name: Overall Equipment Effectiveness
short: A composite measure of equipment availability, performance, and quality.
long: Calculated by multiplying availability, performance, and quality rates. It helps identify whether lost productive time comes from downtime, slow operation, or defects, but comparisons require consistent definitions.

name: Forecast Bias
short: The persistent tendency of forecasts to be systematically too high or too low.
long: Uses signed forecast errors to reveal directional error. A result near zero can still hide large offsetting errors, so bias should be read together with an absolute-error measure.

name: Forecast Error
short: The difference between actual demand and forecast demand for the same period.
long: The sign convention must be stated. Forecast error is the building block for accuracy, bias, MAD, MAPE, and tracking-signal measures.

name: Mean Absolute Deviation
short: The average absolute size of forecast errors.
long: Adds the absolute forecast errors and divides by the number of observations. Because it retains the unit of demand, it is easy to interpret within one item or family.

name: Mean Absolute Percentage Error
short: Average absolute forecast error expressed as a percentage of actual demand.
long: Makes error comparable across different volumes, but becomes unstable or undefined when actual demand is zero or very small.

name: Weighted Absolute Percentage Error
short: Total absolute forecast error divided by total actual demand.
long: Weights errors by volume and avoids averaging individual percentages. The business should define the aggregation level and handling of zero total demand.

name: Tracking Signal
short: Cumulative forecast error compared with a measure of typical absolute error.
long: Often calculated as cumulative error divided by MAD. Values outside agreed control limits can indicate persistent forecast bias requiring investigation.

name: Demand Plan Attainment
short: Actual demand compared with the approved demand plan.
long: Shows how closely realized demand follows the consensus plan at an agreed product, customer, geography, and time level.

name: Forecast Value Added
short: The change in forecast performance produced by a forecasting step or participant.
long: Compares forecast error before and after an activity. Positive value means the step improved the forecast; negative value means it made the forecast worse.

name: Inventory Accuracy
short: The degree to which recorded inventory agrees with physical inventory.
long: Can be measured by location, item, quantity, or value. Tolerances and the definition of a matching record must be consistent.

name: Cycle Count Accuracy
short: The percentage of cycle-counted records found within the accepted tolerance.
long: Tracks the reliability of inventory records using scheduled counts rather than relying only on a full physical inventory.

name: Inventory Value
short: The financial value assigned to inventory held by the organization.
long: May cover raw material, work in process, finished goods, and other classes. Comparisons require a consistent valuation method and reporting scope.

name: Inventory Carrying Cost
short: The cost of holding inventory over a period.
long: Typically includes capital, storage, service, risk, obsolescence, shrinkage, and insurance components, expressed as money or a percentage of inventory value.

name: Excess Inventory
short: Inventory above the quantity justified by current plans, policies, or demand.
long: The threshold should reflect expected demand, lead time, safety stock, lot sizing, and lifecycle status rather than use one arbitrary age for every item.

name: Obsolete Inventory
short: Inventory that is no longer expected to be used or sold normally.
long: Tracks stock made unusable by design changes, expiration, damage, regulation, or lost demand. Financial and physical definitions should be aligned.

name: Slow-Moving Inventory
short: Inventory with usage or sales below an agreed movement threshold.
long: The classification is usually based on time since last movement, expected future demand, or turnover and should account for item lifecycle and seasonality.

name: Stockout Rate
short: The frequency or share of demand occurrences that cannot be served from stock.
long: May be calculated by item, line, order, event, or time. The chosen denominator must be stated because each version answers a different question.

name: Safety Stock Coverage
short: The time or demand coverage represented by safety stock.
long: Relates the safety-stock quantity to average or expected usage, helping planners compare buffers across items while still considering variability and service targets.

name: Raw Material Days of Supply
short: How long current raw-material inventory can support expected consumption.
long: Divides usable raw-material inventory by an appropriate consumption rate. Supplier risk, shelf life, and planned production changes affect interpretation.

name: Finished Goods Days of Supply
short: How long finished-goods inventory can cover expected demand.
long: Converts saleable finished-goods stock into time coverage using forecast or recent demand at a defined aggregation level.

name: Inventory Velocity
short: The speed at which inventory moves through the supply chain.
long: A faster flow generally reduces working capital and response time, but must be balanced with service, variability, and replenishment risk.

name: Available-to-Promise Accuracy
short: How reliably available-to-promise commitments reflect quantities that can actually be delivered.
long: Compares ATP commitments with execution outcomes. Errors may point to inaccurate inventory, supply, lead times, allocations, or order promising rules.

name: Capable-to-Promise Accuracy
short: How reliably capable-to-promise dates and quantities can be executed.
long: Assesses promises that consider capacity and material availability. The promised scope, constraint model, and final delivery result must be aligned.

name: Planning Horizon Coverage
short: How far the approved plan extends relative to cumulative lead time and decision needs.
long: A sufficient horizon should expose future material, capacity, and supplier decisions early enough for action.

name: Planning Data Accuracy
short: The percentage of planning master data that meets defined correctness standards.
long: Can cover lead times, lot sizes, calendars, yields, bills, routings, and policies. Sampling rules and criticality weighting should be documented.

name: MRP Exception Closure Rate
short: The percentage of material-planning exception messages resolved within the target time.
long: Measures disciplined response to reschedule, expedite, defer, cancel, and release signals without assuming every system suggestion should be accepted.

name: Planned Order Release Adherence
short: The share of planned orders released in line with their authorized release dates.
long: Highlights delays or premature releases that can create shortages, excess WIP, or instability. Approved planner overrides should be identified separately.

name: Material Availability
short: The percentage of production requirements with all necessary material available when needed.
long: Usually evaluated at order or operation level. Definitions should cover quality holds, substitutions, allocations, and staged material.

name: Schedule Change Rate
short: The frequency or magnitude of changes made to the production schedule.
long: Tracks additions, cancellations, quantity changes, resequencing, or timing changes within defined time fences.

name: Frozen Zone Change Rate
short: The percentage of scheduled work changed inside the frozen time fence.
long: Shows instability close to execution, where changes are most disruptive. Authorized emergencies should still remain visible rather than silently removed.

name: Resource Load
short: The amount of planned work assigned to a resource over a period.
long: Expressed in hours, units, or another capacity measure and compared with available capacity to identify overloads and underloads.

name: Capacity Load Ratio
short: Required capacity divided by available capacity.
long: A value above 100 percent indicates overload under the current assumptions; a lower value indicates unused capacity or protective capacity.

name: Productive Capacity
short: The effective output capability available for value-producing work.
long: Adjusts theoretical capacity for calendars, planned losses, efficiency, maintenance, and other agreed constraints.

name: Machine Utilization
short: The percentage of available machine time used for production activity.
long: The definition must state whether setup, planned maintenance, waiting, and rework count as utilized time.

name: Labor Utilization
short: The share of available labor time used on defined productive activities.
long: Compares productive or earned hours with available paid hours. Training, absence, indirect work, and planned downtime require explicit treatment.

name: Efficiency
short: Standard output or hours compared with actual output or hours used.
long: Indicates how well a resource performs relative to its standard. It should not be confused with utilization, which asks how much available time was used.

name: Bottleneck Utilization
short: The percentage of available constraint time used effectively.
long: Focuses on the system constraint, where lost time directly limits throughput. Nonproductive running can inflate the number without improving flow.

name: Downtime
short: Time during which equipment or a resource is not available for intended operation.
long: Should be separated into planned and unplanned causes and measured against a clearly defined scheduled-time denominator.

name: Planned Maintenance Percentage
short: The percentage of maintenance hours devoted to planned work.
long: Compares planned preventive, predictive, and scheduled corrective work with total maintenance hours. Higher is not automatically better if necessary corrective work is deferred.

name: Mean Time Between Failures
short: Average operating time between repairable equipment failures.
long: Total operating time divided by the number of failures for a defined asset population and failure definition.

name: Mean Time to Repair
short: Average time required to restore failed equipment to operation.
long: The clock boundaries should state whether diagnosis, waiting for parts, testing, and administrative delays are included.

name: First-Pass Yield
short: The percentage of units completing a process correctly without rework or repair.
long: Good units passing on the first attempt divided by total units entering the process. It reveals hidden rework that final yield can mask.

name: Rolled Throughput Yield
short: The probability that a unit passes every process step without a defect.
long: Calculated by multiplying the first-pass yields of sequential process steps, exposing cumulative loss across the full route.

name: Yield
short: Usable output obtained from a process compared with its input.
long: Can be expressed in units, weight, or another compatible basis. The scope should distinguish first-pass, final, and material yield.

name: Rework Rate
short: The percentage of output requiring additional work to meet requirements.
long: Tracks units or cost sent through corrective processing. Rework should be separated from normal routing and from scrap.

name: Defect Rate
short: The number or percentage of defects relative to inspected output or opportunities.
long: The denominator may be units, transactions, or defect opportunities and must be stated to support valid comparisons.

name: Parts Per Million Defective
short: Defective units expressed per one million units received or produced.
long: Scales a defect proportion for easier comparison when defect rates are low. The inspection and acceptance rules must be consistent.

name: Cost of Quality
short: The combined cost of preventing, assessing, and responding to quality problems.
long: Common components are prevention, appraisal, internal failure, and external failure costs. It makes the economic impact of quality visible.

name: Customer Return Rate
short: The percentage of shipped units or orders returned by customers.
long: Should be segmented by reason, product, customer, and responsibility because not every return indicates a product defect.

name: Supplier Quality Rate
short: The share of supplier receipts meeting defined quality requirements.
long: May use accepted lots, accepted units, defect PPM, or cost. The method should account for inspection intensity and supplier-caused returns.

name: Supplier Fill Rate
short: The percentage of requested inbound units supplied by the vendor.
long: Measures quantity fulfillment at unit level and should distinguish on-time supply from late or partial delivery.

name: Supplier Lead Time
short: Elapsed time from placing a supplier order until the material is available for use.
long: The end point may be receipt, inspection release, or point-of-use availability. Consistent clock boundaries are essential.

name: Supplier Lead-Time Variability
short: The degree to which actual supplier lead times vary around their expected value.
long: Can be expressed with standard deviation, range, or percentile measures and is an important input to safety-stock and promise decisions.

name: Purchase Price Variance
short: The difference between actual purchase price and the planned or standard price.
long: Quantity-weighted variance shows the financial effect of price changes. Currency, freight, duties, and rebates require consistent treatment.

name: Inbound Delivery in Full
short: The percentage of supplier deliveries received in the complete requested quantity.
long: An inbound quantity-completeness measure that can be combined with timeliness to form an inbound OTIF measure.

name: Supplier On-Time In-Full
short: The percentage of supplier deliveries arriving both on time and complete.
long: A delivery passes only if it meets the agreed date or window and the complete quantity requirement.

name: Throughput
short: The rate at which a system generates finished output or goal units.
long: May be measured in units, standard hours, or financial contribution per time period. The definition should reflect the system goal and constraint.

name: Lead Time
short: Elapsed time between initiation and completion of a process or request.
long: Because purchasing, manufacturing, customer, and cumulative lead times use different boundaries, every reported value should identify its start and end events.

name: Queue Time
short: Time work waits before processing begins at a resource or operation.
long: A major non-value-adding component of manufacturing lead time, often driven by large batches, congestion, priorities, or imbalance.

name: Setup Time
short: Time required to prepare a resource to perform a different job or operation.
long: The boundary may include cleanup, tooling, programming, adjustment, and first-piece approval. Internal and external setup should be distinguished.

name: Takt Time
short: Available production time divided by customer demand for the same period.
long: Defines the required production rhythm to meet demand. It is not the same as actual cycle time and changes when demand or available time changes.

name: Cycle Time
short: Elapsed time between successive completions or the time to complete a defined cycle.
long: The exact meaning varies by process, so the measured object, clock boundaries, and inclusion of waiting must be stated.

name: Order Cycle Time
short: Elapsed time from customer order receipt to completed delivery.
long: Measures end-to-end customer response. It may be segmented into entry, planning, production, warehouse, transport, and waiting components.

name: Cash-to-Cash Cycle Time
short: Time between paying for supply inputs and receiving cash from customers.
long: Commonly combines days inventory outstanding plus days sales outstanding minus days payable outstanding.

name: On-Time In-Full
short: The percentage of deliveries that arrive both on time and in the complete quantity.
long: A delivery succeeds only when both timeliness and completeness conditions are met against agreed customer rules.

name: Percentage of Orders Delivered in Full
short: The share of customer orders delivered with every requested item and quantity.
long: Focuses on completeness independently of timeliness. Backorders and substitutions require explicit qualification rules.

name: Delivery Window Compliance
short: The percentage of deliveries arriving inside the agreed delivery window.
long: Treats arrivals before or after the window according to customer rules and uses an authoritative arrival timestamp.

name: Order Entry Accuracy
short: The percentage of customer orders entered without data errors.
long: Can cover product, quantity, price, customer, address, requested date, and terms. Corrections after entry should remain visible.

name: Order Accuracy
short: The percentage of orders fulfilled without item, quantity, documentation, or destination errors.
long: The exact pass conditions should reflect customer expectations and distinguish fulfillment mistakes from later transport damage.

name: Backorder Rate
short: The percentage of demand placed on backorder because it cannot be fulfilled immediately.
long: May use units, lines, or orders as the denominator. Cancellations and substitutions should be tracked separately.

name: Customer Service Level
short: The degree to which inventory or operations meet customer demand as promised.
long: Service level can mean cycle service, fill rate, or another measure. Reports must name the exact formula rather than use the term alone.

name: Customer Complaint Rate
short: Customer complaints relative to shipments, orders, customers, or sales.
long: The denominator and complaint classification must be stable. Severity and recurrence add context that a simple count lacks.

name: Returns Cycle Time
short: Elapsed time from return initiation until final disposition or customer resolution.
long: Can include authorization, transport, inspection, credit, repair, replacement, and disposition stages.

name: Dock-to-Stock Time
short: Elapsed time from receipt at the dock until inventory is available in its storage location.
long: The endpoint should specify whether inventory must also be inspected, recorded, and released for use.

name: Picking Accuracy
short: The percentage of picked items or lines matching the order requirement.
long: Measures correct item, quantity, lot, and other relevant attributes at the chosen unit, line, or order level.

name: Warehouse Space Utilization
short: The share of usable warehouse capacity currently occupied or assigned.
long: May use floor area, cube, pallet positions, or locations. Very high utilization can reduce accessibility and productivity.

name: Labor Productivity
short: Output produced per unit of labor input.
long: Output may be units, standard hours, value, or transactions; labor input may be hours or cost. Mix and complexity should be considered.

name: Multifactor Productivity
short: Output relative to a combined set of resource inputs.
long: Combines labor, capital, energy, materials, or other inputs, normally using value weights to create a consistent index.

name: Total Factor Productivity
short: The efficiency with which all major inputs are transformed into outputs.
long: A broad productivity measure combining weighted labor, capital, energy, material, equipment, and other inputs.

name: Unit Cost
short: The total cost assigned to one unit of product or service.
long: For manufactured items it commonly includes material, labor, and overhead. Comparison requires a consistent volume, costing method, and scope.

name: Cost of Goods Sold
short: The cost assigned to goods sold during a reporting period.
long: Provides the cost basis for gross margin and inventory-turn calculations. Accounting policies determine included manufacturing and acquisition costs.

name: Gross Margin
short: Sales revenue minus cost of goods sold, often expressed as a percentage of sales.
long: Shows the contribution remaining before operating expenses. Mix, transfer prices, discounts, and costing rules affect comparisons.

name: Total Cost to Serve
short: The end-to-end cost of planning, sourcing, producing, fulfilling, and supporting demand.
long: Allocates direct and indirect supply-chain costs to products, customers, channels, or services to reveal true economic performance.

name: Expedite Cost
short: Additional cost incurred to accelerate material, production, or delivery.
long: Includes premium freight, overtime, special handling, and related charges caused by urgent recovery actions.

name: Premium Freight Rate
short: Premium freight cost or shipments relative to total freight activity.
long: Highlights avoidable logistics expense caused by shortages, instability, supplier failure, or late execution.

name: Schedule Attainment
short: The percentage of scheduled production quantity completed in the planned period.
long: Compares actual completed output with scheduled output by item, family, line, or plant and defined time bucket.

name: Production Output
short: The quantity of conforming product completed during a period.
long: Should specify whether reported units are gross, good, transferred, or financially completed and how equivalent units are handled.

name: Order Release-to-Completion Time
short: Elapsed time from production-order release until manufacturing completion.
long: Captures queue, setup, processing, move, inspection, and waiting time after formal release.

name: Production Order Closure Rate
short: The percentage of completed production orders closed within the target time.
long: Timely closure improves inventory, cost, variance, and capacity records while late closure can distort planning signals.

name: Changeover Time
short: Elapsed time from the last good unit of one run to the first good unit of the next run.
long: A consistent boundary captures cleanup, tooling, adjustment, trial production, and approval needed to resume conforming output.

name: Batch Size Adherence
short: How closely executed lot quantities follow authorized batch or lot sizes.
long: Helps reveal unplanned splitting or overproduction while allowing documented responses to demand, yield, shelf-life, or constraint changes.
